revisionNote: Revision 2 adds R07 and cases P01-P02. On 2026-11-09 a separate differential check observed the diagnostic "line-runs: EPIPE: broken pipe, write" on stderr when a downstream reader closed standard output early; GNU uniq 8.32 wrote no diagnostic. R01-R06, G01 and all revision 1 cases are unchanged.
scope: CLI filter on standard input/output. Accept zero arguments or exactly one of -c, -d, -u. Only the declared subset is evaluated.
limits: No file operands, combined or long options, locale-sensitive comparisons, standalone installer, or large-file performance target.
Numeric formatting and byte-level cases are observations from GNU uniq 9.4 in the C locale.
R07 compares stderr only. The exit status after an early close is not compared because GNU uniq ends through SIGPIPE.

criteria.name: Adjacent groups
criteria.acceptance: Emit the first record of each consecutive group in input order. A repeated group after a different line is distinct.

criteria.name: Count
criteria.acceptance: The single -c flag emits one line per group; prepend the decimal count right-aligned to a minimum width of seven, followed by one space.

criteria.name: Repeated groups
criteria.acceptance: The single -d flag emits each group containing at least two lines exactly once.

criteria.name: Single groups
criteria.acceptance: The single -u flag emits only groups with exactly one line.

criteria.name: Record boundaries
criteria.acceptance: LF delimits records. Empty input has no records; an empty line is a record. A final nonempty unterminated record is emitted with LF.

criteria.name: Byte preservation
criteria.acceptance: Compare whole records byte for byte in the C locale. CR, NUL, non-ASCII bytes, and differences in case are data.

criteria.name: Early reader exit
criteria.acceptance: If the reader closes standard output before all output is written, stop reading, write nothing to stderr and end within the case time limit.

criteria.name: Invocation boundary
criteria.acceptance: Reject every option or operand outside the four declared invocation forms. Print no stdout, write a diagnostic to stderr and exit nonzero. This is a local design decision; the reference accepts more invocations.
